limitations: Channel recovery covers account-owned resolved channels; initial historical import and exhaustive channel discovery are not claimed.
Reactions have no method in the pinned layer-135 schema and remain unsupported.
Token renewal commits before activation; mutations interrupted by renewal remain unknown and are never repeated automatically.
Provider search/history/dialog cursors are bound to account and connection; exhaustive pagination and initial import remain unverified.
Not-implemented inventory rows are explicit remaining variants, not a compatibility percentage or a claim of full schema coverage.

Official Web eitaaNoSend explicitly stubs sticker/GIF collection operations, contacts.getTopPeers, reactions and other listed paths; these are absent from native admission even though the TL schema can encode them.
Poll/contact/location incoming message variants project bounded reviewed fields only; raw vCards and private geographic/media access hashes are omitted.

Native OTP/password supports observed account.password2 salted-SHA256 and explicit account.password SRP constructors; delivery metadata comes from provider responses. Native OTP is live-verified on one operator account; password paths remain live-unverified.

Global search uses reviewed searchGlobalExt flags0; exhaustive search/export remain unverified. Finite discussion, invite administration, slow-mode and archive operations have synthetic coverage only.
Read participants implement the pinned scalar Vector<long> response. Current worker UI code expects a newer user/date projection; this alternate server response is not inferred or silently accepted.

Channel deletes and peer/channel cumulative read/content states are projected without fabricated provider dates. Non-channel delete/content updates omit peer on the wire and remain explicit unresolved, gap-marked events.

Private attachment revisions use only actual positive per-update PTS with account or channel scope. Bare history/diff message rows do not inherit page PTS; late unversioned rows cannot prove attachment replacement after an edit/deletion.

Peer IDs are opaque: a classic group uses decimal ID, while a channel-backed supergroup uses channel_<decimal>. This prevents legitimate equal numeric chat/channel IDs from sharing a route, media key or cursor. Restored peer references must match their canonical namespace; no legacy group-ID aliases are accepted.

send.location is static coordinates only; send.contact accepts phone and names with an empty wire vCard. Neither live location, arbitrary vCards nor caller-supplied contact account identity is accepted.
